events.factual_description: Washington Performing Arts presents Hayato Sumino's Chopin Orbit at the Music Center at Strathmore in North Bethesda on Saturday, January 30, 2027 at 7:30 PM. The current event page says Sumino will perform across grand piano, upright piano, and electric keyboard. The published program includes Chopin's Scherzo No. 1, Etude Op. 25 No. 1, Piano Sonata No. 2, Mazurkas Op. 59 No. 1 and Op. 24 No. 2, and the Black Keys Etude; Sumino's Lydian Harp, Big Cat Waltz, White Keys, and Imaginary Polonaise; two explicitly billed improvisations, including one on the ostinato from Chopin's Berceuse; Thomas Ades's Mazurka Op. 27 No. 2; Saint-Saens's Danse Macabre in Sumino's arrangement; and the Stravinsky/Agosti Firebird Suite. Washington Performing Arts identifies this as its introduction of Sumino to D.C. audiences. The authorized Washington Performing Arts ticket page confirms the January 30 date, 7:30 PM time, Music Center at Strathmore, and active seat-selection path, but the checked public page does not expose a stable face-value price. Apple Music lists Chopin Orbit as Sumino's 2026 Classical Crossover album and describes its core idea as pairing Chopin with Sumino's improvisatory reflections and related keyboard works.

en.why_it_matters: Sumino is not treating Chopin as a sealed recital tradition. This program moves among grand piano, upright piano, and electric keyboard, places his own pieces beside Chopin, Ades, Saint-Saens, and Stravinsky, and makes improvisation an explicit part of the architecture. The useful Listening Notes thread is instrumental identity: a Japanese pianist using the classical canon as material for recomposition, timbral contrast, and live invention rather than simply presenting a virtuoso survey.
en.trip_verdict: For the DMV, actively make room for North Bethesda if the January 30 night is open. This is exactly the sort of local appearance worth catching at Strathmore; there is no scarcity reason to turn it into a longer regional trip when the project is part of Sumino's active international orbit.

es.why_it_matters: Sumino no trata a Chopin como una tradición de recital cerrada. El programa se mueve entre piano de cola, piano vertical y teclado eléctrico, coloca sus propias piezas junto a Chopin, Ades, Saint-Saens y Stravinsky, y convierte la improvisación en una parte explícita de la arquitectura de la noche. El hilo útil para Listening Notes es la identidad instrumental: un pianista japonés que usa el canon clásico como material para recomposición, contraste tímbrico e invención en vivo, no simplemente como un recorrido de virtuosismo.
es.trip_verdict: Para el DMV, sí haría espacio activamente para North Bethesda si la noche del 30 de enero está libre. Es exactamente el tipo de aparición local que vale agarrar en Strathmore; no hay una razón de escasez para convertirla en un viaje regional más largo cuando el proyecto forma parte de la órbita internacional activa de Sumino.
